text: A song of ascents. Of David. How good it is, how pleasant, when brothers dwell together in unity!

versions.text: A song of ascents. Of David. How good it is, how pleasant, when brothers live together in unity!
versions.explanation: The verb shevet means 'to sit/dwell,' with the nuance of settled communal life; 'dwell together' is slightly closer to the Hebrew and reads well aloud. Optional refinement — 'live together' is not an error.

text: It is like fine oil poured on the head, running down the beard, down Aaron's beard, running down over the collar of his robes.
It is like the dew of Hermon running down on the mountains of Zion. For there the LORD bestowed his blessing: life forevermore.

versions.text: It is like the dew of Hermon falling on the mountains of Zion. For there the LORD bestowed his blessing: life forevermore.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses the same participle (yored, 'running/coming down') in both verse 2 and verse 3, creating a deliberate verbal link between the oil and the dew. Rendering it 'running down' here preserves that echo for the listener; 'falling' breaks the connection. This is a stylistic refinement only — the current rendering is accurate.
